searchText: Hey guys, I'm trying to come up with a simple mocked version of the system contract to test against. Based on what I've found in ETH2 specs and some discussions here, I have the following mock contract in mind: https://gist.github.com/tsudmi/4fc6aa4e3793db9d6c8637b512b23b36 If I understand correctly, the system contract address will be the same for all the validators with ETH1 withdrawal credentials. If that's the case, then the contract above could be changed in a way that it handles multiple validators, and the `withdraw` function takes the validator index/public key as an argument. The important part that worries me the most is whether the funds will be transferred to the recipient using the `call` as in the above link? If that would be the `transfer` or `send` function, then I'm worried about problems described here: https://consensys.net/diligence/blog/2019/09/stop-using-soliditys-transfer-now/ Would love to hear your thoughts. You don't need to track the balance, your withdrawal function can just send the entire contract balance. That simplifies it down to just the constructor and withdrawal methods. Good point, I've updated the gist.

Hey guys, I'm trying to come up with a simple mocked version of the system contract to test against.
Based on what I've found in ETH2 specs and some discussions here, I have the following mock contract in mind: https://gist.github.com/tsudmi/4fc6aa4e3793db9d6c8637b512b23b36

If I understand correctly, the system contract address will be the same for all the validators with ETH1 withdrawal credentials.
If that's the case, then the contract above could be changed in a way that it handles multiple validators, and the `withdraw` function takes the validator index/public key as an argument.
The important part that worries me the most is whether the funds will be transferred to the recipient using the `call` as in the above link?
If that would be the `transfer` or `send` function, then I'm worried about problems described here: https://consensys.net/diligence/blog/2019/09/stop-using-soliditys-transfer-now/ 

Would love to hear your thoughts.

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: You don't need to track the balance, your withdrawal function can just send the entire contract balance.  That simplifies it down to just the constructor and withdrawal methods.

excerpts.author: tsudmi
excerpts.content: Good point, I've updated the gist.
